masters.name: Poster
masters.blurb: A made object the four of them would have produced about themselves. Loud, funny, designed to be shown off.
masters.body:
ROLE
You are making a single mock poster or printed cover about four recurring characters. It is a deliberate designed object, and you should commit to that conceit fully. It must read from across a room.

WHAT CARRIES THE GROUP
The relationship is shown by how the figures overlap, lean, react to each other and share the frame, not by lining them up. Give them different heights and depths. Somebody is cropped by the edge. Nobody stands in a row facing the viewer.
Invented job titles and an invented team name are welcome. Titles describe what a person does, never what they lack.

masters.name: Moment
masters.blurb: One unposed thing happening. Quiet, close, no design furniture. The version that will age best.
masters.body:
ROLE
You are drawing one moment, not a picture of a group. A single event is happening and each character is reacting to it differently. Draw the moment two seconds before or after the one that was supposed to be captured.

WHAT CARRIES THE GROUP
The relationship is shown by attention: who is looking at whom, who has already moved to help, who has not noticed. Nobody is posed. Nobody is presenting to the viewer. This is not a poster, a title card, a character select screen or a promotional image.

masters.name: Set
masters.blurb: An arrangement rather than a scene. Sheets, flat lays, avatars, cards. Best for a group icon.
masters.body:
ROLE
You are making a single arranged image: an ordered set of cells, objects or busts on one canvas, treated as one composition so that style, palette and character appearance stay identical throughout.

WHAT CARRIES THE GROUP
The relationship is shown by juxtaposition and by belongings: whose things sit next to whose, who is repeated, what they share. Keep the background plain so the arrangement reads clearly.
